summary: An excerpt from a fiction novel (Book 10, part 101) describing CogRad crews deploying wireless connectivity through the Akwesasne woods, where the Warriors and locals warm to the team. Elaine's surveying gear wins over a teenage Warrior called Mermaid, who is given spraychalk to mark sight-lines and later a theodolite, while Lee-Daniel works to engage a man called Cobra by sharing the labor of hauling equipment. The passage closes with a tense exchange with a Series B man about privacy.
one_line: CogRad crews deploy high-speed wireless in the Akwesasne woods, and Elaine and Lee-Daniel win over local Warriors through shared work.
key_facts: CogRad's project in Akwesahsne woods was a real success after treetop-level line-of-sight was achieved.
Within a week, the entire Rez would be unwired at 500 megabits/second.
Elaine unshipped laser-based theodolites and a high-sensitivity digital altimeter during her halts.
The frontmost Warrior, a girl of about 16, later crowded in close to watch Elaine work.
Elaine handed the girl a can of pink spraychalk and directed her to mark the sight-lines.
The girl, called Mermaid, marched off to lay down hot pink lines after recovering from nearly dropping the can.
The rear Warrior, a man of indeterminate age wearing a camou balaclava, rolled his eyes at the spraychalk task.
Lee-Daniel tapped the other Warrior on his shoulder and gestured at a travois carrying the satellite tester.
The other Warrior, called Cobra, took one end of the travois while the juniors looked relieved.
Cobra was a middle-aged man with a handsome face marred by deep acne scars, revealed when he removed his balaclava.
Elaine gave Mermaid a cheap theodolite with an integrated compass, GPS and altimeter, plus a little booklet on how to use it.
Mermaid later led a group of even younger girls on surveying missions around the Indian School.
The CogRad crews had never had explicit training in making friends with locals but learned it from Lee-Daniel and middle-managers.
The Series B man objected to Lee-Daniel's request for privacy, saying the crew was standing all the way over at the far side of the table.
MacDiarmid led the visitors back out to the communal area, after which Lee-Daniel flipped open his notebook.
